title: The Map That Was Wrong On Purpose
real_world_anchor: Cartographers have historically used deliberate map details to detect copying.
script: Some old maps included fake streets on purpose. They were called trap streets, and they helped mapmakers catch copycats. If another company printed the same fake road, it proved they copied the map instead of surveying the city. The clever part is that most people never noticed. A tiny road that did not exist could become courtroom evidence. So the next time a map looks perfectly objective, remember this: sometimes the lie was the signature.
